title: भूपि शेरचनको ‘हामी’ कवितामा सङ्कथन निर्मिति Bhupi Sherchanko "hami" kabitama Sankathan Nirmiti
nepali: प्रस्तुत अनुसन्धानात्मक लेखमा कवि भूपि शेरचनको ‘हामी’ कवितालाई पाठकारूपमा लिई त्यसमा सङ्कथन निर्मितिका विभिन्न पक्षहरूको विश्लेषण र मूल्याङ्कन गरेरउक्त कविताको अर्थ निक्र्यौल गरिएको छ । ‘हामी’ कवितामा सङ्कथन निर्मितिहरू कसरीवितरित भएका छन् र तिनको अन्तर्सम्बन्धबाट उक्त कविताको आशय निर्धारण गर्नु यसलेखका उद्देश्य हुन् । यसमा सङ्कथन विश्लेषणका अध्येता जेम्स पल गीले स्थापना गरेका सातप्रकारका सङ्कथन निर्मितिका आधारभूत मान्यतालाई सैद्धान्तिक ढाँचाका रूपमा अवलम्बनगरी पाठगत विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यसमा प्राकृतिक वस्तु र मानवीय सहभागीहरूका निरर्थक क्रियाकलापहरूको दृष्टान्तहरूबाट तार्किक शृङ्खलाको सुसंयोजन गरी ‘हामी’ कवितामामानवीय अभिमान र यथार्थबिचको भिन्नताप्रति तीक्ष्ण व्यङ्ग्य एवम् अनस्तित्वमा पनिअस्तित्वको सम्भावना खोजी गरिएको छ भन्ने निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: In this research article, taking the poet Bhupi Sherchan's poem 'Hami' ('We') as a text, the meaning of that poem is drawn out by analysing and evaluating various aspects of narrative construction (sankathan nirmiti) within it. The objectives of this article are to determine how narrative constructions are distributed in the poem 'Hami' and to fix the import of the poem through their interrelation. In this, textual analysis has been carried out by adopting as a theoretical framework the basic propositions of the seven types of narrative construction established by James Paul Gee, a scholar of narrative analysis. In this, a logical sequence has been composed out of illustrations of natural objects and the futile activities of human participants, and the conclusion has been reached that in the poem 'Hami' there is a sharp satire on the gap between human pride and reality and a search for the possibility of existence even in non-existence.
british_english: The present research article takes the poet Bhupi Sherchan's poem 'Hami' as a text and, by analysing and appraising the various aspects of narrative construction within it, draws out the meaning of that poem. The aims of this article are to establish how narrative constructions are distributed in the poem 'Hami' and to determine the purport of the poem through their interrelation. In this, textual analysis has been undertaken by adopting as a theoretical model the fundamental tenets of the seven kinds of narrative construction set out by James Paul Gee, a scholar of narrative analysis. In this, a logical sequence has been composed out of instances of natural objects and the futile activities of human participants, and the conclusion has been reached that in the poem 'Hami' a keen irony towards the disparity between human conceit and reality, and a quest for the possibility of existence even within non-existence, have been pursued.
australian_english: This research article takes the poet Bhupi Sherchan's poem 'Hami' as a text, weighing up and commenting on the different sides of narrative construction in it, and in that way nails down what the poem means. The aims of this article are to pin down how narrative constructions are spread through the poem 'Hami' and to settle the poem's import from how they hang together. In it, the close reading is done by taking on, as a theoretical frame, the basic assumptions behind the seven types of narrative construction laid out by narrative analysis scholar James Paul Gee. In it, by stringing together a logical run from examples of natural objects and the pointless carryings-on of human participants, the conclusion is drawn that the poem 'Hami' makes a sharp send-up of the gap between human big-headedness and reality and goes looking for the possibility of existence inside non-existence too.
informal_english: This research piece treats Bhupi Sherchan's poem 'Hami' as a text and, by sifting through and sizing up the different bits of how the story's put together in it, works out what the poem's really saying. The point of the article is to nut out how those narrative constructions are spread across 'Hami' and to settle what the poem's getting at from the way they all fit together. For that, the close reading leans on the basics of the seven kinds of narrative construction set out by narrative analysis bloke James Paul Gee, using them as a theoretical frame. Along the way, by lining things up in a logical run using examples of natural objects and people's pointless mucking about, it wraps up that 'Hami' takes a sharp dig at the gap between human big-noting and reality and hunts for a bit of existence even in non-existence.
translator_notes: Source is a literary analysis of Bhupi Sherchan's 'Hami' poem; narrative construction concept (sankathan nirmiti) and seven types by James Paul Gee preserved; sentence order kept intact.
